g.text: The full interval section determines R
s has degree −1; the crossing differential is −κ.
C_Y = Y₁ ⊕ sY₀ → C_X = X₁ ⊕ sX₀
y₁ ↦ Σ₁y₁
sy₀ ↦ sΣ₀y₀ + R(y₀)
R = pr_X₁ ∘ Σ_cyl ∘ s
All original parameter components are included.
Its chain equation gives both endpoint terms
δR = κ_X Σ₀ − Σ₁ κ_Y
J = (Q₁κ_X − κ_YQ₀)H₀ + Q₁RQ₀
δJ = Q₁κ_X − κ_YQ₀
The original section value is JΣ₀ = Q₁R.
Exact model: a necessary two-parameter core
M₀(y) = f + z
M₁(sa; y) = z
M₂(sa | sb; y) = 2z
dc = a − E_uf; |sa| = |sb| = 0
Delete M₂ while keeping κ_X fixed:
chain defect at sc | sb ⊗ y is +2z.
Object and one-parameter cores remain unchanged.
Whole interval and projection equations: Theorem 48, (48.1)–(48.8).
Explicit graded matrix/bar model and defect: Exercise 48.
Marked-Yoneda orientation and normalization: Theorems 24–27, 43.
